headline: UN talks on killer robots end with no binding rules
pages: Diplomats at the United Nations in Geneva agreed early Saturday to begin discussing options for regulating lethal autonomous weapons, often called killer robots. The week of talks ran into the small hours before a compromise emerged. Countries will have two years to suggest regulations, which could be legally binding but could also be optional. Negotiators said the deal was better than nothing and showed the UN disarmament process can still work. Many humanitarian groups and governments said it falls well short. The International Committee of the Red Cross had urged binding rules within a year, a call backed by the UN secretary-general and Pope Leo. Their concern comes from current wars.

In Sudan, the UN says drones caused 80% of civilian deaths this year, and aid groups fear AI-assisted weapons could soon decide to kill without human control. Why it matters: rules on autonomous weapons are being debated while the technology is already in use. Source: NPR.
